newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - FX vols tiptoe lower, curves stay flat.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FX vols tiptoe lower, curves stay flat.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar-pair options tiptoed lower as nervousness prevailing after last week's wild spot movements gave way to time-decay concerns in quiet U.S. trading, dealers said.
"Basically, dollar/mark and dollar/yen are consolidating after huge moves on Friday," said Soma Rao, first vice president and options sales manager at Smith Barney.
Still, volatility curves for most major currency pairs, perhaps except dollar/Swiss franc, remained flat as traders were wary of selling gamma-rich shorter maturities.
"Right now people are not really eager to sell (options) because they expect the market to move," said a U.S. bank trader in the West Coast. "Nobody really wants to go short gamma in this market."
Negative gamma positions, typically a result of selling shorter-dated options, benefit from time decay but are vulnerable to spot market gyrations.
Dollar/mark implied volatilities from one-month out to one-year stood at around 11.1/11.3 percent in early afternoon U.S., off about 0.2 point across the curve from late Monday levels.

News of the Bundesbank's 3.0-percent fixed rate repo tender briefly buoyed the dollar but had negligible lasting impact on the market. There had been speculation the central bank might set a variable rate tender to let money market rates rise -- a thinly veiled effort to support the mark.
The spot dollar drifted in the mid-1.86 mark area for most of the U.S. morning.

In dollar/yen, one-month volatility lost nearly half a point to 11.4/11.6 percent, while one-year was off a quarter point at 11.6/11.8 percent, as spot clawed back up from early lows in the mid-115 yen area.
Traders said many market participants were staying on the sidelines ahead of Wednesday's July U.S. retail sales and producer price index and Thursday's consumer price index.

While those indicators were unlikely to prompt the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates at the August 19 Federal Open Market Committee meeting, strong numbers could send the U.S. stock and bond markets into a tailspin again, traders said.
They said Friday's dollar selloff of four yen and nearly four pfennigs was triggered by a tumble in asset markets linked to inflation concerns.

Sterling volatilities were little changed, with one-month cable at 10.2/10.6 percent and one-month sterling/mark at 11.9/12.3 percent. The cable curve was flat but sterling/mark was clearly inverted as spot tumbled below 2.95 marks again.
Dollar/Swiss-dollar/mark volatility spreads were near zero, if not slightly negative, in the front end. Traders said spot dollar/Swiss had been lagging dollar/mark lately.

But the spread in the one-year area was at about a full point in favor of Swiss, closer to usual levels. The West Coast trader said strong interest in the back end had been the common factor among most currencies in recent weeks.
